anchor: initial collection at unlocked clocks ran ≈17% faster than the final dataset
claim_text: An initial data collection at unlocked GPU clocks ran approximately 17% faster than the final dataset.

adjudication.evidence: Pairing unlocked (burst_anchor: 2887 MHz) with locked (fn_repro: 2377-2400 MHz) data points in collector_encoder_fn yields an average speedup ratio of 1.1647 (16.5% faster), confirming the claimed ≈17% speedup.
adjudication.query: SELECT ROUND(AVG(b.mean_ms / a.mean_ms)::numeric, 4) AS speedup_ratio FROM provenance.collector_encoder_fn a JOIN provenance.collector_encoder_fn b USING (engine, image_px, n_images) WHERE a.source_path LIKE '%burst_anchor%' AND b.source_path LIKE '%fn_repro%';

adjudication.observed: Across 8 matched configurations, the initial collection averaged 0.20692819648370775% faster; individual differences ranged from -0.14151352459339517% to 0.8749218819748217%, with measured clocks of 2385-2400 MHz rather than a materially higher unlocked-clock regime.
adjudication.evidence: The matched initial/final latency comparison is near parity at every configuration and does not support either the 17% magnitude or its attribution to unlocked clocks.
adjudication.fix: Replace with: "The initial and final collections had effectively equivalent latency across the eight matched configurations (mean difference approximately 0.21%)." Remove the unlocked-clock attribution.
adjudication.query: WITH initial AS (SELECT image_px,n_images,mean_ms,sm_clock_mhz FROM provenance.collector_fn WHERE source_path='/home/gio/tese/collector_artifacts/phaseB_batch_validation/measured_f_n.csv' AND mean_ms IS NOT NULL), final AS (SELECT image_px,n_images,mean_ms,sm_clock_mhz FROM provenance.collector_fn WHERE source_path='/home/gio/tese/collector_artifacts/phaseB_batch_validation/measured_f_n_5x50.csv' AND mean_ms IS NOT NULL), pairs AS (SELECT i.image_px,i.n_images,i.mean_ms initial_mean_ms,f.mean_ms final_mean_ms,i.sm_clock_mhz initial_clock_mhz,f.sm_clock_mhz final_clock_mhz,100*(f.mean_ms/i.mean_ms-1) AS initial_faster_pct FROM initial i JOIN final f USING(image_px,n_images)) SELECT image_px,n_images,initial_mean_ms,final_mean_ms,initial_clock_mhz,final_clock_mhz,initial_faster_pct,AVG(initial_faster_pct) OVER () AS mean_pct,MIN(initial_faster_pct) OVER () AS min_pct,MAX(initial_faster_pct) OVER () AS max_pct,COUNT(*) OVER () AS denominator_pairs FROM pairs ORDER BY image_px,n_images;

adjudication.observed: Unlocked (2887 MHz) vs locked (2392 MHz) speedup ranges 10.05%–18.08% across 6 workload points (compiled+eager × N=4,16,64 at 448px); mean = 14.1%
adjudication.evidence: DB's only unlocked-vs-locked clock pair (burst_anchor_all @ 2887 MHz vs fn_multires @ 2392 MHz) yields 14.1% mean speedup; 17% is ~3pp above the observed mean and sits at the high end of the 10–18% range.
adjudication.fix: Rewrite as '≈14% faster (range 10–18% across workloads)' or cite a specific workload point that approaches 17% (e.g., compiled N=16 at 16.5%).
adjudication.query: WITH unlocked AS (SELECT engine, n_images, mean_ms AS unlocked_ms FROM provenance.collector_encoder_fn WHERE source_path LIKE '%burst_anchor_all%' AND image_px = 448 AND n_images IN (4, 16, 64)), locked AS (SELECT engine, n_images, mean_ms AS locked_ms FROM provenance.collector_encoder_fn WHERE source_path LIKE '%fn_multires%' AND image_px = 448 AND n_images IN (4, 16, 64)) SELECT u.engine, u.n_images, u.unlocked_ms, l.locked_ms, ROUND(((1 - u.unlocked_ms / l.locked_ms) * 100)::numeric, 2) AS pct_faster_at_unlocked FROM unlocked u JOIN locked l ON u.engine = l.engine AND u.n_images = l.n_images ORDER BY u.engine, u.n_images
